newsitem.title: ITALY: French judge questions Algerian suspect in Italy.
newsitem.headline: French judge questions Algerian suspect in Italy.

text.p: French anti-terrorist investigator Jean-Louis Bruguiere flew to Italy on Wednesday to question an Algerian suspected of supplying arms to Moslem guerrillas, judicial sources said.

Bruguiere arrived in Naples where he was due to question Djamelk Lounici, who is suspected of ties to the armed wing of the Algerian Islamic Salvation front (FIS), at the southern port city's Poggioreale prison, the sources said.
Lounici, 34, was arrested in Italy in May 1995 and is due to go on trial in Naples next April on charges of smuggling arms to Moslem guerrillas in Algeria.
He is also awaiting extradition to France where he is being tried in absentia with 33 fundamentalists accused of backing Moslem guerrillas in Morocco.
The 33 were among nearly 200 Moslem fundamentalists detained after a wave of bomb attacks in France in 1995 in which eight people were killed and 160 injured.
Bruguiere, France's top anti-terrorism investigating magistrate, has led high-profile probes into terrorists around the world including into jailed guerrilla mastermind "Carlos the Jackal".

He is due to meet magistrates in Turin on Thursday to discuss their "operation Shakba" in which 19 people were arrested in the northern city last month on suspicion of belonging to an Algerian terrorist network, the sources said.
